{{Quote|Legendary for their stupidity and curiosity — have been known to wander onto and accidentally stow away on visiting spacecraft.|[[Lyrre T'enna]]'s notes on the Nuna|<ref name=":3" />}}
'''Nuna''', commonly called '''swamp turkeys''',<ref name=":3">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> were [[Reptavian/Legends|reptavian]] [[Hunting/Legends|gamebirds]] native to [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] that spread to many other planets. They were exported all around the galaxy for use as pets, meat, egg layers, or  curiosities.<ref name=":3" />

Subspecies include the common nuna and the dwarf nuna.<ref name=":3" />

==Anatomy==
[[File:Nuna_Skeleton.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Nuna Skeleton]]
Nuna were diminutive bipeds, mostly covered in scaly skin and sporting a distinctive dorsal ridge. They came in a variety of shades, ranging from [[Color/Legends|greens]]<ref name=":3" /> to browns,<ref name=":2" /> depending on the subspecies. They possessed a notably prominent jutting jaw and two large wattles hanging from either side of their mouths. They had large three-toed feet which were quite massive with respect to the rest of their bodies. Though the nuna were flightless, their skeletons were [[Bird/Legends|birdlike]], as evidenced by a large keel-bone and pelvis. Distinctively, they featured a large anterior body cavity that the male nunas could inflate when agitated.<ref name=":3" /> Furthermore, the females laid one egg that was huge for the creature's size, which could contain up to ten chicks. Apparently, the temperature influenced the sexual determination of the eggs.<ref name=":3" />

A dwarf subspecies existed, known as dwarf nuna, the adult of which was approximately the same size as a chick of the common species. This small subspecies also had a darker green skin than the common nuna.<ref name=":3" />

==Behavior==
[[File:Nunachicks-woswfg.jpg|thumb|right|200px|Nuna hen and chicks]]
Nuna often exhibited awkward behavior, running with more of a waddle than a stride on their long legs. When vocalizing, a nuna's wattles erected outwards from their face. When angered or agitated, the male nuna could inflate its body to a strikingly larger size, similar to the coexisting [[Gullipud]].<ref name=":3" /> Nuna survived on a primary diet of swamp plants, though they exhibited opportunistic omnivorous behavior, occasionally eating [[Worm/Legends|worms]] and other small invertebrates.<ref name=":3" /> Although they were non-aggressive, they could effectively defend themselves with kicks from their powerful clawed legs when cornered.<ref name="NunDB" /> Nuna also exhibited a high reproductive rate, laying considerable batches of [[Egg/Legends|eggs]] that also acted as a decent fertilizer if not hatched.<ref name=":3" />

Nunas were heavily preyed upon by other creatures but flourished due to their fast running, ability to adapt, [[Disease/Legends|disease]] resistance, and sheer fruitfulness. Young common nuna could be eaten by [[Pikobi/Legends|pikobis]].<ref name=":3" />

==History==
===Origins and Spread===
[[File:Nuna_CW.png|thumb|left|200px|Nuna were common throughout the galaxy.]]

Nuna were common in the [[Gungan Swamp|swamps]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]],<ref name=":2" /> notably in the [[Lianorm Swamp/Legends|Lianorm Swamp]].<ref name="JPB guide">[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Jedi Power Battles'': Prima's Official Strategy Guide]]</ref> It is unknown how or when the nuna evolved on Naboo. It is understood, in part, how they spread to other planets. A number of dwarf nunas were exported to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] as pets of [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba Desilijic Tiure]], who enjoyed flicking them off great heights, callously killing the creatures.<ref name=":2">{{Film|I}}</ref> Over time, the imported population apparently escaped captivity and large numbers of wild dwarf nunas dwelt invasively in the deserts during the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. Nuna eventually spread to other planets, including [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]]<ref name=":1" /> and [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]],<ref name="Senate Murders">{{TCW|Senate Murders}}</ref> where they were considered vermin,<ref name="NunDB" /> game,<ref name=":0" /> and household pets.<ref name=":3" />

===Sports===
As a pastime, Naboo [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] were known to use nunas in their bloated, agitated state for sport, kicking them around like balls. "[[Nuna-ball/Legends|Nuna-ball]]" would gain some interest in the rest of the galaxy after the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]]. Thus arose another cause of galactic emigration as nunas were exported to many worlds to meet demand for nuna-ball. On some worlds, nunas were even raced in betting matches. The [[Committee Against Non-Sentient Abuse]], an organization that protested the mishandling of animals, raised its voice against Nuna-ball matches for their misuse of nunas.<ref name=":0">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|50|sports/1344_1.html|Nuna-Ball League Looks to Expand}}</ref>

===Culinary Use===
[[File:Roast_nuna.png|thumb|right|220px|A roast nuna being carved]]
{{Quote|Deep-fried nuna leg mmm. Delicious!|[[Orn Free Taa/Legends|Orn Free Taa]]|<ref name="Voyage of Temptation">{{TCW|Voyage of Temptation}}</ref>}}
Nuna apparently had made it as a dish as far away as [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]]<ref name="The Deserter">{{TCW|The Deserter}}</ref> by [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]]<ref name="Annual">''[[Star Wars Annual 2011]]''</ref> as evidenced by [[Clone Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Rex/Legends|Rex's]] encounter with one at a [[Cut Lawquane/Legends|farmer's]] dinner table.<ref name=":1">{{TCW|The Deserter}}</ref>

Many dishes used Nuna for its meat, including [[Nuna Gumbo/Legends|Nuna Gumbo]],<ref name="MIA">{{TCW|Missing in Action}}</ref> [[Nuna drumstick/Legends|Nuna drumsticks]],<ref name=":1" /> [[Nuna bacon]], [[Nuna sausage]], and the [[Nuna salad sandwich]].<ref name="Dining at Dex's">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/dexdiner/index.html|text=Dining at Dex's|int=Dining at Dex's}}</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
The nunas first appeared in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars:'' Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace video game">[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]]</ref> and made their cinematic debut in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars:'' Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']].<ref name="Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace">{{Film|I}}</ref> They were created by concept artist [[Terryl Whitlatch]]. The nuna was a comical favorite, and was eventually transplanted off [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] to [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], becoming an omnipresent "[[Rat/Legends|rat]]" of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]].<ref name="NunDB">{{DB|creature|nuna|nuna}}</ref>

The nuna was developed to essentially be the ''Star Wars'' equivalent of a turkey.
